text:
Evan (AE): Hey team — finserv prospect wants a short POC but with strict EU-only residency and no sub-processors in Russia/Belarus. They also want KMS keys in their Azure tenant and a routing guarantee that traffic never leaves EU. Can we confirm feasibility + rough cost delta vs standard hosted?
Priya (SE): short answer: doable but two paths: 1) Hosted + tenant pinning + regional endpoints (soft guarantee w/ routing policy + SAML/KMS handoff) or 2) Dedicated VPC/Private deployment (hard isolation, more $).
Marco (Eng): technical bits: we can pin tenant to eu-west-1 cluster and set routing policy to prefer eu models. fallback behavior: if eu capacity exhausted, policy can either queue, failfast, or route to a compatible EU model in eu-central-1 — not to non-EU. No automatic cross-border fallback.
Evan (AE): they explicitly said no cross-border even for fallback. Must be hard reject or failover within EU only.
Marco (Eng): ok we can enforce a strict region allowlist. Need to confirm subprocessor list for eu-region infra (cloud provider + redis/pg managed services).
Jenna (Ops): will need ~2 weeks to spin a dedicated tenant pin + KMS integration for POC if we avoid Dedicated hardware. Private deployment would be longer (4-6 weeks) and needs contract.
Evan (AE): pricing question: any ballpark for a 4-week POC with 50k tokens/day? They expect no long-term commit during POC.
Priya (SE): ballpark: Hosted with strict EU routing + BYOK KMS: add 20-30% regional compliance surcharge + per-token. Tenant pinning includes a small config/setup fee. Dedicated Private (reserved capacity) would be a monthly minimum (higher) — I can run numbers.
Evan (AE): pls do. Also: they asked about sub-processors — legal wants an up-to-date list and attestations for EU-only.
LegalBot: automated note: subprocessor list available at https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors (includes cloud provider locations). For contract-level attestation, escalate to Legal; add SOW addendum for EU-only subprocessors.
Marco (Eng): two technical caveats: 1) third-party observability tools may forward traces (we can opt-out or host on EU tenant) 2) some vendor kernels (quant library) are from a US OSS maintainer — that source code doesn't process customer data but check if customer flags that.
Priya (SE): to summarize options for customer: a) Hosted EU-only routing + BYOK KMS + region allowlist (fastest, moderate cost) b) Dedicated reserved capacity in EU (highest isolation, higher cost & longer lead) c) Private deployment in customer's VPC (full control, enterprise contract).
Evan (AE): next steps? customer wants an ops checklist for POC and an updated quote by Fri EOD.
Jenna (Ops): I'll draft the ops-runbook template (network egress checklist, KMS handshake steps, certs) — target Thu.
Priya (SE): I'll produce two quotes: 1) Hosted EU-locked POC (no commit) with setup fee + surcharge, 2) Dedicated 1-month trial estimate. Also will include config snippet for tenant routing policy.
Priya (SE): ```
routing_policy:
  tenant_pin: true
  allowed_regions: ["eu-west-1", "eu-central-1"]
  fallback: failfast
  kms: "customer-byo-kms"
```
Evan (AE): Nice. Do we need Legal signoff before we send the POC quote?
LegalBot: for any attestation referencing subprocessor restrictions, attach Data Residency Addendum. Legal review required only if they request contractual carveouts beyond our standard addendum.
Evan (AE): I'll ask the customer to confirm if addendum needed.
Marco (Eng): one more ops note: for strict EU enforcement we'll add a per-tenant network ACL + egress verification job during the POC. Cost: small infra delta.
Jenna (Ops): ops handoff: @Priya -> once quote approved, I'll schedule environment prep (2x infra tickets: tenant-pin + kms-binding).
Priya (SE): ack. I'll upload the quote + tech note to the deal room and ping here when done.
Evan (AE): thanks all. Owners: Priya (quote & tech note), Jenna (ops runbook & infra tickets), Marco (eng signoff on routing policy), Legal will standby.
Priya (SE): ETA for quote: Fri 17:00 UTC.
Jenna (Ops): ETA runbook draft: Thu 12:00 UTC.
Evan (AE): perfect. I'll schedule demo for next Tue provisional. :thumbsup:
